entries.test: Musk's public predictions from 2015 through May 2022 and the autonomous driving capabilities commercially available by May 2022 would settle this.
entries.note: The normalization turns “pretty much” every year into an exceptionless annual claim.

entries.test: Public studies comparing perceived AI capability after demonstrations dominated by common cases versus demonstrations including rare cases could test the claimed misleading effect.
Published evaluations of contemporary data-driven AI on common and rare cases would show whether rare events caused substantial performance failures in May 2022.
entries.note: “Rather than reasoning” strengthens “more on big data than on reasoning.”

entries.test: Public technical descriptions of Tesla's May 2022 driving systems and investigations of their unexpected-situation failures could test the asserted mechanism and causal link.
entries.note: The normalization drops “so far as I know” and makes the lookup analogy more literal. “Hence” explicitly asserts causation.
“Probably” makes the forecast probabilistic. “The bane” does not establish a ranking as the single main weakness.

entries.test: Tesla's delivery records and documented vehicle capabilities would establish whether it shipped any SAE Level 5 cars during 2022 or 2023.
Published methods and robustness evaluations available by May 2022 would establish whether a broadly robust solution to AI outlier failures was known.
Public evidence of AGI achieved while retaining heavy dependence on the techniques current in 2022 would refute the asserted necessity of moving beyond them.
entries.note: In context, he predicts a technical necessity for achieving AGI. The normalization recasts it as an unconditional research prescription and drops “current techniques like.”
The extracted outlier forecast retains the explicit “might” qualification.

entries.test: Public evaluations available in May 2022 comparing deep learning's reliability relative to human performance across object recognition, planning, reading, and language comprehension would test the comparison.
Published 3D perception and scene-understanding evaluations through May 2022 would establish whether substantial unresolved failures remained.

Public robustness evaluations for common sense, reasoning, language, and analogy from approximately 2017 through May 2022 would test both the absence of dependable solutions and the claimed lack of change.
entries.note: The comparison concerns dependable general capabilities, rather than the absence of any benchmark gains.
The passage assesses a research approach and advocates additional techniques. “Will not be a panacea” strengthens “seems pretty unrealistic to me.”
The normalization omits the qualification that invention is necessary only if the tools do not already exist. “Might well” is probability language.

entries.test: Public evaluations of the range of cognitive tasks required for general domestic robotics versus road driving could test the asserted difference in required generality.
entries.note: He explicitly disclaims knowing the plans for Optimus; the normalization identifies it as a general-purpose domestic robot.

entries.test: Public engineering methods and deployment results through May 2022 would show whether complex cognitive systems could be built and modified reliably without recurring integration failures.
entries.note: The following paragraphs explain adequacy in terms of integration, debugging, and avoiding regressions.

entries.test: Publicly documented AGI achieved without resolving the described integration and debugging problems would refute the necessity claim, while proposals available in May 2022 would test its present-tense component.
entries.note: This combines an undated necessity forecast with an observation about existing proposals.

entries.test: Published interpretability research, debugging methods, and controlled debugging studies available by May 2022 would test the claimed limitations and their contribution to debugging difficulty.
entries.note: The normalization drops “really” and narrows the open-ended “and so forth” to data and layers alone.
The predicted necessity is explicitly qualified by “probably.” The separate present-tense assertion about verification tools is checkable.

entries.test: Public evaluations in 2029 of AI watching movies and accurately explaining their events, characters, conflicts, and motivations would settle the forecast.
Public evaluations in 2029 of AI answering questions about novels, including questions requiring inference beyond the literal text, would settle the forecast.
entries.note: The normalization omits the explicitly essential requirement to go beyond the literal text.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent evaluations in 2029 of AI robots competently cooking in varied unfamiliar kitchens would settle the forecast.

Public independent evaluations in 2029 of repeated AI generation of bug-free programs exceeding 10,000 lines from natural-language specifications or non-expert interaction, excluding library assembly, would settle the forecast.
Public evaluations in 2029 of AI formalizing arbitrary natural-language proofs drawn from mathematical literature into representations suitable for symbolic verification would settle the forecast.
entries.note: The normalization broadens the domain by omitting “from the mathematical literature.”
